intent.raw_query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February

experiences.name: Zermatt Ski Safari
experiences.description: Explore the legendary slopes of Zermatt with access to over 360km of groomed pistes beneath the iconic Matterhorn. Take the Gornergrat cogwheel railway to reach high-altitude runs and enjoy varied terrain suitable for all skill levels, with breathtaking panoramic views of 29 peaks over 4000m.

experiences.name: Verbier Freeride Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided off-piste freeride session in Verbier, one of the world's top freeride destinations. A certified mountain guide leads you through untracked powder fields and challenging couloirs in the Mont Fort area, offering an adrenaline-packed adventure for intermediate to advanced skiers.

experiences.name: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Tour
experiences.description: Ride the cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m, the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace carved inside the glacier, walk on the Aletsch Glacier, and enjoy stunning views of the surrounding Alpine peaks. A once-in-a-lifetime mountain experience combining culture and nature.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening
experiences.description: Warm up after a day on the slopes with a traditional Swiss cheese fondue dinner at a cozy mountain chalet restaurant in Grindelwald. Enjoy locally sourced Gruyère and Emmental cheeses paired with Swiss wines and regional bread, immersing yourself in authentic Alpine culinary culture.

experiences.name: Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail
experiences.description: Glide through 100km of perfectly groomed Nordic trails around Davos, the highest city in Europe. This full-day cross-country skiing experience takes you through pristine snow-covered forests and frozen lakes, with optional instruction from a local Nordic coach for beginners and intermediates.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich or Milan Malpensa airport at 22:30. Take a pre-booked budget train or bus transfer toward Poschiavo. The Bernina Express or regional train via Tirano connects to Poschiavo. Check in to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama, settle in, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Grab a quick sandwich or snack at the airport or train station convenience store (CHF 5–10) before the journey to Poschiavo

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your train ticket in advance via SBB.ch for the best budget fares. The journey from Zurich to Poschiavo takes approximately 3.5–4 hours via Chur and the Bernina line. Keep luggage light for easy train travel. Confirm B&B late check-in arrangements ahead of time.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. Enjoy a hearty B&B breakfast included with your stay. Take a leisurely morning walk around the charming historic village of Poschiavo — explore the Piazza Comunale, the Spanish Quarter (Quartiere Spagnolo), and the Reformed Church. The village is compact and walkable, offering stunning Alpine winter scenery at no cost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Lago di Poschiavo (Lake Poschiavo), a short walk or free bus ride from the village center. In winter the lake area offers beautiful frozen or misty scenery. Explore the lakeside trail on foot or rent snowshoes locally (approx. CHF 15–20/day) for a gentle introductory winter hike along the valley floor.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo village for dinner. Stroll the illuminated historic streets and plan your ski days ahead by checking local ski area maps and lift pass prices at the B&B.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B Berninahaus Panorama — enjoy local bread, cheese, and cold cuts
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a local Poschiavo bakery or Coop supermarket (CHF 8–12) — try local Pizzoccheri bread or a panino
meals.dinner: Ristorante Albrici in Poschiavo — a historic local restaurant offering traditional Graubünden dishes like Pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta) and Capuns. Budget meal approx. CHF 18–25

day_by_day.notes: Poschiavo is in the Italian-speaking part of Graubünden, so menus and locals speak Italian. The village is a UNESCO World Heritage site as part of the Rhaetian Railway landscape. Pick up a local SBB regional day pass (approx. CHF 20–30) for unlimited bus and train travel in the valley.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Bernina Express train (approx. CHF 10–15 one way with regional pass) up to Pontresina or St. Moritz area — the train ride itself is a world-class scenic experience through the UNESCO Bernina Pass. Arrive at Pontresina and head to the Diavolezza ski area (accessible by cable car from Bernina Diavolezza station). Purchase a half-day ski lift pass (approx. CHF 45–55) for a budget-friendly ski morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Diavolezza — the area offers spectacular glacier views of Piz Palü and Piz Bernina. Intermediate and beginner runs are available. Rent ski equipment at the base if needed (approx. CHF 35–45/day for skis, boots, and poles). Take the iconic Diavolezza glacier run in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Poschiavo via the Bernina line. Relax at the B&B and warm up with a hot shower. Head out for a budget dinner in the village.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B
meals.lunch: Self-service mountain restaurant at Diavolezza — bring your own packed snacks and thermos of hot tea/coffee to save money (CHF 0–5). Or budget cafeteria soup and bread (CHF 12–15)
meals.dinner: Osteria della Posta in Poschiavo — cozy local osteria with affordable pasta and risotto dishes (CHF 15–22). Try the local Graubünden barley soup (Gerstensuppe)

day_by_day.notes: Diavolezza lift pass: check for midweek discounts or afternoon passes to save CHF 10–15. The Bernina train pass is included if you have a Swiss Travel Pass or regional day pass. Book ski rental in advance online for 10–15% discount. Dress in warm layers — temperatures at Diavolezza (2,978m) can drop to -15°C in February.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning train up the Bernina Pass to Pontresina. From Pontresina, join a guided snowshoe tour through the Roseg Valley — one of the most beautiful and accessible winter valleys in the Alps. Guided tours are available through local operators (approx. CHF 25–35 including snowshoe rental) or self-guided with rented snowshoes (CHF 15–20). The valley offers views of the Roseg Glacier and surrounding 4,000m peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Roseg Valley snowshoe loop (approximately 3–4 hours total). Stop at the historic Romantik Hotel Roseg-Gletscher horse-drawn sleigh station for a hot chocolate (CHF 5–7). Return to Pontresina on foot or by horse-drawn sleigh (approx. CHF 15–20 per person for the sleigh ride — a memorable budget splurge).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Pontresina village briefly before catching the train back to Poschiavo. Pontresina has a charming main street with local shops. Return to B&B for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from Coop in Poschiavo before departure — sandwiches, fruit, and energy bars (CHF 8–10). Eat in the scenic Roseg Valley
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using groceries from Poschiavo's Coop supermarket — pasta with local cheese and cured meats (CHF 8–12 total). Use the B&B kitchen if available, or pick up ready-made items

day_by_day.notes: The Roseg Valley is car-free in winter, making it exceptionally peaceful. The snowshoe trail is well-marked and suitable for beginners. Wear waterproof boots and gaiters. The horse-drawn sleigh to the Roseg Hotel is a classic Engadin experience worth the small extra cost. Check train times carefully — service frequency decreases in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Full ski day at Corvatsch ski area near Silvaplana/St. Moritz — accessible by train to Silvaplana and then local bus (approx. CHF 12–18 round trip with regional pass). Corvatsch offers excellent intermediate and advanced skiing at 3,303m with stunning Engadin lake views. Purchase a full-day lift pass (approx. CHF 65–75 — look for online advance purchase discounts of 10–15%).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing Corvatsch's varied terrain. The area connects to Furtschellas above Sils Maria, offering additional runs and quieter slopes away from the St. Moritz crowds. Take the panoramic cable car to the summit for breathtaking 360-degree Alpine views even if you rest your legs briefly.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by train. This is a longer ski day so arrive back by 19:00–20:00. Treat yourself to a well-earned sit-down dinner at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B — eat a large breakfast for energy on the slopes
meals.lunch: Bring a packed lunch in a backpack to eat on the mountain (CHF 8–10). Most ski areas have designated picnic areas. Supplement with a hot soup at the mountain restaurant (CHF 8–10)
meals.dinner: Ristorante Suisse in Poschiavo — local Swiss-Italian cuisine with fondue and raclette options. Budget CHF 20–28 per person. Raclette is a perfect après-ski meal

day_by_day.notes: Corvatsch is one of the highest ski areas in the Engadin and can be very cold and windy — bring a balaclava and hand warmers. Friday may be busier as weekend visitors arrive. Start early (first lift at 08:30) to beat crowds. The Engadin ski pass covers multiple areas including Corvatsch, Corviglia, and Diavolezza — if planning multiple ski days, a multi-day pass (3-day approx. CHF 180–200) offers better value than single-day tickets.

day_by_day.morning: Take the scenic Bernina Express train to Tirano, Italy (approx. 45 minutes, CHF 10–15 one way) — the train crosses the famous Brusio spiral viaduct, a UNESCO World Heritage engineering marvel. Spend the morning exploring the charming Italian border town of Tirano, visiting the Basilica della Madonna di Tirano (free entry) and the historic town center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Browse the local Italian market stalls and shops in Tirano for affordable Italian food products, wine, and souvenirs. Stock up on Italian pasta, cheese, and local Valtellina wines at significantly lower prices than Switzerland. Return to Poschiavo by early afternoon. Spend the afternoon on a final snowshoe or winter walk along the Val Poschiavo valley trail near the B&B, enjoying the quiet mountain scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Poschiavo. Enjoy a final evening in the village, visiting the local bar for a glass of regional Valtellina wine or a Grappa. Walk the illuminated historic streets one last time.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B
meals.lunch: Lunch in Tirano, Italy — significantly cheaper than Switzerland. A full pasta meal at a local trattoria costs EUR 10–14 (approx. CHF 10–15). Try Pizzoccheri della Valtellina, the regional buckwheat pasta specialty
meals.dinner: Self-catered farewell dinner using Italian groceries purchased in Tirano — quality pasta, local cheese, salumi, and wine (CHF 15–20 total for a feast). Eat at the B&B if kitchen facilities are available

day_by_day.notes: Bring your passport for the Italy day trip — even within the Schengen Area, border checks occasionally occur. The Brusio spiral viaduct is best photographed from the train — sit on the right side heading toward Tirano. Italian prices are 30–50% lower than Swiss prices for food and wine, making this an excellent budget shopping opportunity. The Bernina railway is one of the steepest non-rack railways in the world — an incredible engineering experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final B&B breakfast. Pack and check out. Take one last short walk around Poschiavo village to soak in the Alpine atmosphere. Visit the local Sunday market if operating. Head to the train station and begin the journey home via the Bernina Express to Chur, then onward to Zurich airport or your departure point. The morning Bernina train offers spectacular winter light on the glaciers and mountain passes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Train journey through the Swiss Alps — Poschiavo to Chur (approx. 2.5 hours) then Chur to Zurich (approx. 1.5 hours). Total journey approximately 4 hours. Enjoy the final Alpine scenery from the panoramic train windows. Arrive at Zurich in time for afternoon/evening flights.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Zurich or continue onward travel. If time permits before your flight, explore Zurich's old town (Altstadt) briefly — it's a 10-minute train ride from the airport.

meals.breakfast: Final included B&B breakfast — eat well for the journey
meals.lunch: Train station Migros or Coop To Go in Chur — affordable Swiss sandwiches, salads, and hot drinks (CHF 10–15)
meals.dinner: Airport food or on the plane. Alternatively, grab a budget meal at Zurich HB (main station) — Manor Food Hall or Migros restaurant offers hot meals from CHF 12–16

day_by_day.notes: Book your return train tickets in advance on SBB.ch for the best prices. The Bernina Express reservation costs CHF 10–14 extra but is worth it for the panoramic carriages. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight departure when traveling from Poschiavo to Zurich Airport. The Swiss Travel Pass (if purchased) covers all train travel including the Bernina line, making it excellent value for a 7-day trip. Total estimated budget for the week excluding flights and accommodation: CHF 350–500 per person, covering transport, lift passes, meals, and activities.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Settle into your room and rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama around midnight. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's sleep to prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — travel day
meals.lunch: Grab a bite at the airport or on the plane before landing
meals.dinner: Light snack from airport or convenience store upon arrival — most restaurants will be closed by arrival time

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport transfer in advance. The B&B is located in Poschiavo, a scenic Romansh-speaking valley town near the Bernina Pass. Confirm late check-in with the property ahead of time. Pack light layers for the cold alpine night air.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the B&B. Take a morning orientation walk through the charming village of Poschiavo — explore the historic Piazza Comunale, the Spanish-style houses, and the frozen Lake Poschiavo nearby. Get your bearings in this beautiful Graubünden valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Livigno or Diavolezza ski area (Diavolezza is approximately 30–40 minutes from Poschiavo via the Bernina Pass road). Spend the afternoon on the slopes at Diavolezza, a stunning glacier ski area with breathtaking views of Piz Palü and Piz Bernina. Rent ski equipment on-site if needed. Suitable for intermediate skiers.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo for a relaxed evening. Stroll the village and warm up at a local café or wine bar with a glass of Graubünden Pinot Noir.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — enjoy local bread, cheese, cold cuts, and coffee
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant at Diavolezza ski area — try a hearty Rösti with cheese or a warming soup (CHF 18–28)
meals.dinner: Ristorante Suisse or a local trattoria in Poschiavo — enjoy regional pasta, polenta, or braised meat dishes (CHF 25–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check road conditions on the Bernina Pass before driving — it can be icy in February. Diavolezza day ski pass costs approximately CHF 60–70. Dress in warm, waterproof layers. Sunscreen is essential at altitude even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Board the iconic Bernina Express (or regional Rhaetian Railway train) from Poschiavo toward St. Moritz — one of the most scenic rail journeys in the world, a UNESCO World Heritage route. Arrive in St. Moritz and explore the glamorous resort town on foot, visiting the frozen Lake St. Moritz and the village center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hit the slopes at Corviglia, St. Moritz's main ski mountain, accessible by funicular from the town center. Enjoy over 350km of connected ski runs in the Engadin ski region. The views of the Engadin valley from the top are spectacular. Ski until late afternoon before catching the train back to Poschiavo.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the B&B after a full day. Optional: enjoy a soak or rest, then head out for a quiet dinner in Poschiavo.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the B&B before departing
meals.lunch: Self-service mountain restaurant at Corviglia — try Engadiner Nusstorte (walnut tart) and a warm soup or pasta (CHF 20–30)
meals.dinner: Osteria Salis in Poschiavo — a beloved local spot serving traditional Graubünden cuisine including pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta) and venison (CHF 25–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Rhaetian Railway from Poschiavo to St. Moritz takes about 1 hour and is extremely scenic — sit on the right side heading north for the best views. A regional day pass for trains and ski lifts (Engadin combo) can offer good value. Book train tickets in advance during peak ski season.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Tour — depart early from Poschiavo by train toward Interlaken (approximately 3–3.5 hours via Chur or St. Moritz). From Interlaken, take the cogwheel train up to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m, the highest railway station in Europe. Marvel at the Aletsch Glacier, the Sphinx Observatory, and panoramic views of the Bernese Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ice Palace, walk on the glacier plateau, and enjoy the surreal snowy landscape at the Top of Europe. Take photos with the iconic Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks as your backdrop. Begin the descent back toward Interlaken in the mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey toward Poschiavo — this is a long travel day. Arrive back at the B&B by late evening. Enjoy a simple dinner in Poschiavo or pick up provisions for a cozy in-room meal.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the B&B before departing
meals.lunch: Crystal Restaurant at Jungfraujoch — enjoy a warm meal at the top of Europe with stunning glacier views (CHF 25–40); alternatively pack snacks to save budget
meals.dinner: Pizzeria or casual café in Poschiavo upon return — pizza, pasta, or a simple plat du jour (CHF 18–28)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long but unforgettable day trip. The Jungfraujoch excursion ticket costs approximately CHF 145–175 (with Swiss Travel Pass discounts available). Book tickets in advance online. Altitude sickness can affect some visitors at 3,454m — take it slow and stay hydrated. Dress in your warmest layers as temperatures at the top can be -15°C or colder.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the big Jungfraujoch day. Enjoy a slow breakfast at the B&B. Take a peaceful snowshoe walk or winter hike around Lake Poschiavo — the frozen lake and surrounding snow-covered forests are magical in the morning light. Rent snowshoes locally if needed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take the train to Pontresina (approximately 40 minutes from Poschiavo), a charming alpine village near St. Moritz. Enjoy the Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail experience — while Davos itself is farther, the Engadin Nordic ski network around Pontresina and St. Moritz offers over 200km of perfectly groomed cross-country trails. Glide through pristine winter landscapes at a gentler pace than downhill skiing.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening experience — find a cozy mountain chalet restaurant in Pontresina or St. Moritz for a traditional Swiss cheese fondue dinner. Warm up with melted Gruyère and Emmental cheese, crusty bread, and a glass of white wine or hot tea.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the B&B
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or café stop in Pontresina — try a Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup) and bread at a local bakery (CHF 12–18)
meals.dinner: Traditional Swiss fondue dinner at Chesa Pontresina or a similar mountain chalet restaurant — fondue set menu approximately CHF 35–50 per person including bread and salad

day_by_day.notes: Cross-country ski rental in Pontresina costs approximately CHF 25–35 per day. The Engadin Nordic trails are well-marked and suitable for all levels. The fondue evening is best enjoyed as a social, leisurely meal — don't rush it! Pontresina is a quieter, more affordable alternative to St. Moritz for dining.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the Zermatt Ski Safari — depart early from Poschiavo toward Zermatt (approximately 3–3.5 hours by train via Chur and Visp). Arrive in the car-free village of Zermatt and take the gondola up to the legendary slopes beneath the iconic Matterhorn. Begin skiing the vast 360km network of groomed pistes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Zermatt Ski Safari — explore different sectors of the mountain including Rothorn, Gornergrat, and Klein Matterhorn (the highest ski point in the Alps at 3,883m). The views of the Matterhorn from the slopes are absolutely iconic. Ski until late afternoon before heading back down to the village.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Zermatt village in the early evening — browse the charming pedestrian streets, pop into a mountain shop, and enjoy the festive après-ski atmosphere. Take the train back toward Poschiavo, arriving late evening.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the B&B before departing
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant on the Zermatt slopes — try a Zermatt specialty like Älplermagronen (alpine macaroni with cheese and applesauce) or a hearty soup (CHF 22–35)
meals.dinner: Grab dinner in Zermatt before the return train — try Whymper-Stube for traditional Swiss cuisine or a mid-range restaurant on the main street (CHF 28–45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is car-free — take the electric taxi or walk from the train station. A Zermatt ski day pass costs approximately CHF 85–95. Book train tickets in advance as Saturday trains can be busy. This is a long but spectacular day — the Matterhorn views make it absolutely worth it. Consider a Swiss Travel Pass for savings on train travel throughout the week.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Take a final walk through Poschiavo village to soak in the atmosphere — visit the local Sunday market if available, pick up Swiss chocolates, Bündner Nusstorte, or local wine as souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, enjoy one last activity: a scenic drive or train ride along the Bernina Pass for stunning winter mountain photography, or a short beginner-friendly ski session at Diavolezza. Begin packing and preparing for departure. Check out of the B&B.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to the airport (Zurich or Milan Malpensa are the nearest major airports — approximately 2.5–3 hours). Enjoy a final Swiss meal at the airport or en route. Depart with incredible memories of the Swiss Alps.

meals.breakfast: Final full breakfast at the B&B — savor the local cheeses, meats, and fresh bread one last time
meals.lunch: Café or restaurant in Poschiavo or en route to the airport — try a Capuns (Swiss chard rolls with spätzle) or a simple sandwich (CHF 15–22)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or en route dining — budget CHF 20–35 for a final Swiss meal

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the B&B. Allow extra travel time to the airport in winter due to potential road or rail delays. Zurich Airport (ZRH) is the most common departure hub — approximately 2.5 hours by train from Poschiavo via Chur. Milan Malpensa (MXP) is approximately 2.5 hours by car. Buy Swiss chocolate and local Graubünden specialties as gifts before leaving!

day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival at 22:30. Light welcome amenities at the B&B — enjoy a glass of local Valposchiavo wine and a charcuterie board prepared by the host. Rest and prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (travel day)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (in transit)
meals.dinner: Light in-room welcome board arranged by the B&B — local cured meats, Graubünden dried beef (Bündnerfleisch), artisan cheeses, and Poschiavo valley bread with a bottle of regional Pinot Noir.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private luxury transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar) from Zurich or Milan Malpensa airport to Poschiavo. The drive from Zurich is approximately 2.5 hours; from Milan Malpensa approximately 2 hours. Confirm late check-in with the B&B in advance. Pack ski gear or arrange rental for the following days.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the B&B with panoramic Alpine views. After breakfast, explore the charming historic village of Poschiavo on foot — stroll through the Spanish Quarter (Quartiere Spagnolo) with its colorful Italianate mansions, visit the Collegiate Church of San Vittore, and soak in the serene winter atmosphere of this UNESCO-recognized cultural landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Diavolezza ski area (approx. 30–40 min drive via the Bernina Pass road), one of the most spectacular glacier ski areas in the Alps. Enjoy afternoon skiing on the Diavolezza glacier with breathtaking views of Piz Palü and Piz Bernina. Hire a private ski guide for a personalized introduction to the terrain. Rent premium ski equipment on-site if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo for a refined dinner at Ristorante Suisse or Albergo Croce Federale — both offer elevated regional cuisine. Enjoy Pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with local cheese and vegetables), slow-braised venison, and a curated selection of Graubünden wines.

meals.breakfast: Full Alpine breakfast at B&B Berninapass — fresh bread, local jams, Bündnerfleisch, soft-boiled eggs, yogurt with mountain honey, and freshly brewed coffee with panoramic valley views.
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch at Diavolezza summit restaurant — enjoy hearty Rösti, Alpine soup, and hot chocolate at 2,978m elevation with jaw-dropping glacier panoramas.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Suisse, Poschiavo — regional Graubünden cuisine featuring Pizzoccheri, braised venison with polenta, and a bottle of Malanser Pinot Noir.

day_by_day.notes: Diavolezza is accessible via the Bernina Express road or by taking the Rhaetian Railway to Pontresina and then the Diavolezza cable car. A private car or taxi is recommended for flexibility. Check snow and weather conditions before heading up. Lift passes can be purchased on-site or online in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Board the iconic Bernina Express (Rhaetian Railway) from Poschiavo station for a scenic morning journey through the UNESCO World Heritage Bernina line — crossing dramatic viaducts, glaciers, and snow-covered Alpine passes. Arrive in St. Moritz (approx. 45 min) — the crown jewel of luxury Alpine resorts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Zermatt Ski Safari Experience (adapted to Corviglia/St. Moritz ski area for the day): Engage a private ski instructor and explore the world-class Corviglia ski area above St. Moritz — 350km of immaculate pistes, stunning Engadine valley views, and perfectly groomed runs for all levels. Enjoy the legendary St. Moritz ski culture with access to exclusive mountain clubs.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening at a cozy mountain chalet restaurant in St. Moritz — Chesa Veglia (a 17th-century farmhouse restaurant) is the quintessential luxury choice, offering traditional cheese fondue, raclette, and fine Swiss wines in an intimate, candlelit setting. Return to Poschiavo by private transfer.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast before departure — fresh pastries, local cheeses, cold cuts, fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at El Paradiso mountain restaurant on Corviglia — a legendary St. Moritz institution with panoramic Engadine views, serving truffle pasta, grilled meats, and premium wines.
meals.dinner: Chesa Veglia, St. Moritz — traditional Swiss cheese fondue and raclette in a historic 17th-century farmhouse setting. Reserve well in advance. Pair with a Fendant du Valais white wine.

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express train from Poschiavo to St. Moritz is a world-class scenic journey — book first-class panoramic seats in advance through the Rhaetian Railway website. Return to Poschiavo via private luxury transfer in the evening (approx. 45 min). St. Moritz lift passes can be purchased at the Corviglia cable car base station.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Tour: Depart early by private transfer to Grindelwald or Interlaken (approx. 2.5–3 hours from Poschiavo). Board the cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m — the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace, Sphinx Observatory, and the eternal snow plateau with awe-inspiring views of the Aletsch Glacier, the longest glacier in the Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: After descending from Jungfraujoch, enjoy a premium afternoon skiing session at Grindelwald First ski area — a spectacular high-altitude ski domain with views of the Eiger North Face. Hire a private guide for a curated run selection across the First and Männlichen areas.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium restaurant in Grindelwald before the return transfer to Poschiavo. The Michelin-recognized Restaurant Firestarter at Hotel Belvedere or the elegant dining room at Grand Hotel Regina offer exceptional Alpine cuisine. Return to Poschiavo by private luxury transfer.

meals.breakfast: Early B&B breakfast before departure — light and energizing with fresh bread, eggs, yogurt, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Jungfraujoch Crystal Restaurant at 3,454m — a truly once-in-a-lifetime dining experience above the clouds. Enjoy warm Alpine soups, pasta, and hot beverages.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Firestarter, Hotel Belvedere, Grindelwald — contemporary Alpine cuisine with premium ingredients, featuring dishes like Bernese lamb, truffle risotto, and a curated Swiss wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Jungfraujoch tickets must be booked well in advance — purchase the 'Good Morning Ticket' for early access and lower pricing. The round trip from Grindelwald takes approximately 3–4 hours including exploration time. Dress in very warm layers as temperatures at 3,454m can be extreme. Altitude sickness is possible — take it slowly upon arrival at the summit.

day_by_day.morning: Verbier Freeride Experience: Depart by private transfer to Verbier (approx. 2.5–3 hours from Poschiavo). Join a guided off-piste freeride session in Verbier — one of the world's top freeride destinations and home of the legendary Freeride World Tour. A certified IFMGA mountain guide will lead you through Verbier's iconic off-piste terrain including the Vallon d'Arby and Mont Gelé couloirs (terrain matched to your skill level).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Verbier's 410km of ski terrain with your private guide. Access the Mont Fort glacier at 3,330m for high-altitude powder runs and panoramic views across four countries. Enjoy the vibrant après-ski culture at Verbier's legendary mountain bars.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski at the iconic Farm Club or Pub Mont Fort in Verbier — the heartbeat of Verbier's luxury social scene. Dinner at Restaurant La Grange au Feu or the Michelin-starred Rosalp for an exceptional fine dining experience before the return transfer to Poschiavo.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast before early departure — hearty and warming with eggs, local cheeses, cold cuts, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Cabane du Mont Fort (3,330m) — a legendary high-altitude mountain hut serving hearty Alpine fare including Croûte au fromage, soups, and warming Glühwein with extraordinary panoramic views.
meals.dinner: Restaurant La Grange au Feu, Verbier — rustic luxury Alpine dining featuring Valais beef fondue, raclette with local Valais cheeses, and an extensive Swiss and French wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: Verbier freeride terrain is for intermediate to advanced skiers. Inform your guide of your exact skill level in advance so the experience is tailored appropriately. Avalanche safety equipment (beacon, probe, shovel) is provided by the guide. Book the IFMGA guide through Verbier's Bureau des Guides at least 2 weeks in advance. Return transfer to Poschiavo is approximately 2.5–3 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail Experience: Depart by private transfer to Davos (approx. 1.5 hours from Poschiavo). Glide through 100km of perfectly groomed Nordic trails around Davos — the highest city in Europe at 1,560m. Hire a private Nordic ski instructor for a guided tour through the stunning Flüela and Dischma valleys, passing frozen lakes and pristine snow-covered forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Nordic morning, transition to downhill skiing at Parsenn — one of Switzerland's largest and most prestigious ski areas, shared between Davos and Klosters. Enjoy the legendary Weissfluhjoch runs and the famous 12km Parsenn Derby descent with a private ski guide.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Davos's finest restaurants — Bündnerstube at Steigenberger Grandhotel Belvédère offers exceptional Graubünden regional cuisine in an elegant Belle Époque setting. Enjoy Capuns (Swiss chard rolls with spätzle), Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup), and premium Graubünden wines before the return transfer to Poschiavo.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast before departure — full Alpine spread with fresh bread, local honey, Bündnerfleisch, cheeses, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bergrestaurant Weissfluhjoch (2,844m) on the Parsenn — panoramic mountain restaurant serving Rösti, Alpine soups, and warm beverages with sweeping views over Davos and the Graubünden Alps.
meals.dinner: Bündnerstube, Steigenberger Grandhotel Belvédère, Davos — elegant regional Graubünden cuisine in a historic grand hotel setting. Pair with a bottle of Malanser Completer or Pinot Noir.

day_by_day.notes: Nordic ski equipment rental is available at the Davos Nordic Center near the Flüela trailhead. Classic and skate skiing styles are both available — specify your preference when booking the instructor. The Parsenn ski area lift pass is separate from the Nordic trails. A combined day pass covering both is available at the Davos tourist office.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — enjoy a leisurely, indulgent breakfast at the B&B with panoramic views of the Bernina massif. Take a peaceful morning walk through the snow-covered streets of Poschiavo's historic center, visiting the weekly Sunday market if available. Browse local artisan shops for Graubünden specialties — Bündner Nusstorte (walnut tart), local wines, and handcrafted souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last afternoon ski session at Diavolezza glacier (30–40 min from Poschiavo) — a perfect farewell to the Swiss Alps with one final run on the glacier beneath Piz Bernina. Alternatively, enjoy a relaxing spa afternoon at a nearby luxury wellness facility in Pontresina or St. Moritz (Kempinski Grand Hotel des Bains offers exceptional spa facilities).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the finest restaurant in Poschiavo or a short drive to Pontresina — Ristorante Albergo Croce Federale in Poschiavo or the elegant dining room at Hotel Saratz in Pontresina. Celebrate an extraordinary week in the Swiss Alps with a premium tasting menu and a bottle of vintage Graubünden Pinot Noir. Pack and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury farewell breakfast at B&B Berninapass — full spread with fresh pastries, local cheeses, Bündnerfleisch, smoked salmon, eggs, fresh fruit, yogurt with mountain honey, and a celebratory glass of Prosecco.
meals.lunch: Light mountain lunch at Diavolezza summit restaurant or a picnic-style lunch prepared by the B&B with local specialties to enjoy on the slopes.
meals.dinner: Hotel Saratz, Pontresina — elegant fine dining featuring a seasonal tasting menu with Engadine and Graubünden ingredients, paired with a curated wine flight. A perfect luxury farewell to the Swiss Alps.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the B&B and arrange luggage storage if needed for the afternoon activities. Book the farewell dinner reservation at Hotel Saratz well in advance as it is popular on weekends. Arrange the departure transfer in advance — whether returning to Zurich Airport, Milan Malpensa, or another hub. The Bernina Express also offers a scenic departure option back toward Chur or St. Moritz for onward connections.
